verses.text: David talked things over with his commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and with every one of his leaders.

Then he said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If you think it is good, and if it is the will of the LORD our God, let's send word to our relatives everywhere in all the land of Israel. Let's also send word to the priests and Levites in their towns with pasturelands, so they can come and join us.
Then let's bring the ark of our God back to us, because we did not care about it while Saul was king."
The whole assembly agreed to do this, because everyone thought it was the right thing to do.
So David gathered all Israel, from the Shihor River in Egypt to Lebo Hamath, to bring God's ark from Kiriath Jearim.

David and all Israel went up to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim in Judah. They went to bring back the ark of God the LORD, who sits on his throne between the cherubim, the ark that is called by his name.
They carried God's ark on a new cart from Abinadab's house, and Uzza and Ahio were guiding the cart.
David and all the Israelites were celebrating before God with all their strength, singing and playing harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, the oxen stumbled, and Uzza reached out his hand to steady the ark.
The LORD became very angry with Uzza, and he struck him down because he had touched the ark. So Uzza died there in front of God.
David was angry because the LORD had burst out in anger against Uzza. That place is still called Perez Uzza today.
David was afraid of God that day. He asked, "How can I ever bring God's ark home with me?"
So David did not take the ark with him into the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-Edom from Gath.
God's ark stayed with Obed-Edom's family in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his family and everything he had.
